datasetVersion: pickle-real-v0.1 (+2 cases: rally2 dev, afn-vic held-out)
protocol: DETECTOR-ONLY on identical labeled frames; hit radius 0.08 normalized; ±40ms match tolerance; a 'claim' is any racket-class detection in the matched frame. No tracker, no ownership gating.

candidates.license: Apache-2.0 code + Apache-2.0 weights (N/L family; XL/2XL are PML — excluded)
candidates.verdict: NOT PROMOTED — no recall gain, 32% slower, adds a dependency

headlineFinding: THE PADDLE DETECTOR IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK. The frozen COCO-proxy detector finds the paddle in 27/27 visible labeled frames (including the bright paddle and the motion-blurred overhead previously reported as 'detector failures'). End-to-end paddle P/R is 0.37 — meaning ~63% of available detection quality is destroyed downstream by OUR tracking, ownership gating, window/span selection and confidence gates, not by the model.
correctionOfPriorClaims: Earlier sessions attributed bright-paddle and blurred-overhead misses to the COCO proxy; measurement shows the detector saw them. The misses are tracker/association failures.

Earlier in THIS session an intermediate RF-DETR run reported P/R 0.00 due to a class-id mapping bug (COCO_CLASS_NAMES list index vs COCO_CLASSES dict id). Fixed before scoring; the 0.00 numbers were never valid.
nextExperiments: 1. Tracker/association ablation: measure P/R after each stage (raw dets → tracks → ownership gate → window gate) to localize the 63% loss exactly. Highest expected return of any model work.
2. Only after that: consider a pickleball-specific detector fine-tune.
3. Precision (0.68) is limited by other players' paddles — an OWNERSHIP problem, already the top labeled-data gap.
